title: The Charleston dance craze and a gang leader friend
summary: After knocking down the neighborhood tough he became friends and danced the Charleston with him on corners.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: I know during that period that I was down there in the sixties it was, like, -- this dance -- the Charleston, was out during that period.

And, I made a friend with one of the guys in the neighborhood, who was supposedly the baddest guy in the neighborhood. And I think then we had a fight one day. And after awhile, I just -- I think I kind of knocked him down. And everybody was amazed that I did that to -- -- you know what I mean, him. (laugh) including me and the bad guy.

So, ever since that, he and I were real close friends. And he was the leader of the gang on the block, you know. So, we used to go around on different corners -- that's when the Charleston was out -- and I -- as I say, I could always dance. And he had a ukelele, and we used to go on corners and dance, and uh --
Well, we ought to get these, this straight for just the time, because --
Yeah, I was thinking for a minute -- Why was the "Charleston" called the "Charleston". Do you know?
Did it have anything to do with Charleston?
It didn't originate in Charleston, did it?
I don't know. I don't remember why -- I don't know
It probably did though, you know?
Why would it be called that. It probably did.
Maybe you brought it up and didn't know.
Well, Freddie. If you were, say like, fourteen then?
So, that was about 1924, say. Or 1923.
I didn't know the "Charleston" came out that early.
Yes. When I came uh that's what it was It came out -- I swear to God -- 1923.
